# v0.5 animation clips, frame counts, and pose recovery

## What is recovered

For every `AnimationSet`, v0.5 retains:

- clip name
- first track + track count
- source key count
- first/last animation tick
- recovered integer-tick frame count
- optional authored `AnimTicksPerSecond`

For every `Animation`, it retains:

- track name
- target Frame name
- resolved stable Frame ID
- first key + key count

For every key, it retains:

- authored time/tick
- raw key type
- normalized semantic (rotation/scale/position/matrix)
- compatibility flags
- original Q16.16 values

## No fixed clip/frame ceiling

The library does not define a maximum number of clips or animation frames.
Storage is supplied by the caller. A first counting pass can use NULL arrays:

```c
xp_anim_capture count;
xp_anim_requirements req;

xp_anim_capture_init(&count, 0,0, 0,0, 0,0, 0,0);
xp_anim_capture_callbacks(&cb);
/* xp_parse(..., &cb, &count); */
xp_anim_capture_get_requirements(&count, &req);
```

The caller then provides `req.nodes`, `req.clips`, `req.tracks`, and `req.keys`
records from static storage, an arena, a VFS-owned buffer, or another allocator
outside this library. The decoder itself performs no allocation.

## Frame count

`.x` animation keys contain a positive DWORD time measured in ticks. Therefore
v0.5 exposes a deterministic integer-tick runtime timeline:

```text
frame_count = last_tick - first_tick + 1
frame_index = 0 .. frame_count-1
tick        = first_tick + frame_index
```

This is exact for assets authored with one animation frame per tick (including
the tested dog and Zombie Apocalypse models). If a file uses a higher tick
resolution, use `ticks_per_second` when present to resample to the renderer's
playback FPS.

Microsoft references:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/direct3d9/animationkey
- https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/direct3d9/timedfloatkeys

## Random access

```c
xp_anim_local_pose scratch[MY_RIG_NODE_CAP];
int tick;

r = xp_anim_sample_pose_frame(
    &anim,
    clip_index,
    frame_index,
    scratch,
    MY_RIG_NODE_CAP,
    &tick
);
```

After `XP_OK`, `scratch[i]` contains the complete local pose for Frame node `i`.
Nodes not animated in that frame retain their bind local matrix.

## Stream all clips and poses

`xp_anim_emit_all_poses()` walks:

```text
clip 0
  frame 0
    node 0 pose
    node 1 pose
    ...
  frame 1
    ...
clip 1
  ...
clip N
```

Only one `node_count`-sized pose scratch array is required. Frames are not
cached internally, so a clip can contain thousands or millions of timeline
frames without a pose-memory multiplier.

## Sampling policy

- position: fixed-point linear interpolation
- scale: fixed-point linear interpolation
- rotation: shortest-path normalized quaternion lerp (`w,x,y,z`)
- matrix keys: exact matrix on authored key ticks; between sparse keys, hold the
  preceding matrix and set `XP_ANIM_POSE_MATRIX_HELD`
- before the first source key of a channel, use its first key
- after the last source key, use its last key
- unanimated Frames retain the authored bind local matrix

The raw keys remain available, so a runtime may replace these sampling policies
without losing source information.
